summary: Feed s173_triple to IDS is degraded with 3 active faults: 18.5% duplicates, 86% encrypted bytes vs 60% IDS tolerance, and 1.78 Gbps microbursts overloading 1 Gbps tool port (7 intervals). IDS wastes capacity on copies, is blind to most payloads, and will drop packets on bursts, significantly reducing detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Duplicate packets from aggregated SPAN/mirror feeds or overlapping TAPs fed to same broker without deduplication; 507 of 2742 packets (18.5%) are copies exceeding 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes cycles reprocessing same packets, inflates connection state, risks duplicate alerts/false positives and reduces effective inspection capacity for unique traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop copies before the IDS, restoring capacity and alert fidelity without losing unique traffic.

findings.root_cause: 86% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC) vs IDS tolerance of ~60%; traffic is forwarded encrypted without out-of-band decryption, leaving IDS with no payload to inspect.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature and anomaly detection but is blind to 86% of traffic, missing exploits, C2 and malware inside encrypted streams.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt relevant TLS centrally at the packet broker or route encrypted flows to a decryption-capable inspection zone so the IDS receives cleartext it can analyze; do not attempt inline decrypt on the IDS itself.

findings.root_cause: Microburst peaks of 1.78 Gbps in 1ms intervals exceed the 1 Gbps IDS port (178% of capacity, 7 overloaded intervals); single-tool feed cannot absorb aggregate burst rate.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS port buffers overflow and drop packets during bursts, causing missed flows, incomplete sessions and gaps in detection despite no broker drops yet.

recommended_fix.why: Spread traffic across 2+ IDS members with flow-aware load balancing to keep per-tool peaks below 80% of 1 Gbps and eliminate burst loss.
